_meta.description: Live macro themes affecting currencies but not on the scheduled news calendar. Update as regime-changing events happen. Scanner reads this at brief generation time and displays it in the daily/weekly review.
_meta.howToUse: Each theme should include: (1) short title, (2) start date, (3) currency implications with brief reasoning, (4) a specific watchLevel that would invalidate the theme, (5) affectedPairs for scanner correlation. Retire themes by moving to _retired[] with an endDate.

themes.title: Canada-US trade war LIVE — Section 338 50% tariffs operative since Aug 22; Canada C$27.6B retaliation effective 12:01am Sept 8 (TONIGHT); US counter-response unknown; Trump 50% auto tariff threat Jan 1 2027
themes.summary: As of September 7, the Canada-US trade war reaches its next hard inflection point tonight: Canada's C$27.6 billion, 700+ tariff-line retaliatory package takes effect at 12:01 a.m. September 8 — a binary that has been building since trade negotiations formally collapsed the night of August 21-22. The US Section 338 50% tariffs on C$27.6 billion of Canadian goods have been operative since August 22, covering dairy, alcohol, building materials, electronics, apparel, and agricultural goods, with no CUSMA exemption and no statutory expiry. Canada's Department of Finance confirmed the full counter-tariff list on August 25-26 at rates of 15%, 25%, and 50% matched to US Section 338 and Section 232 rates. Sectors targeted include steel and aluminum (duties doubled to 50%), dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, plastics, and electronics, covering $27.6 billion CAD in US imports. Canadian Finance Minister Champagne also announced a C$7.5 billion business support package alongside the counter-tariff list. Trade negotiations collapsed on August 21-22, with USTR Greer saying Canada 'wanted more' than Washington was willing to offer, while PM Carney said US terms were 'neither fair nor economically sound.' Expert commentary from New York Law School noted both sides 'have now committed themselves in public, which is how escalation stops being a choice.' No evidence of diplomatic reopening or US intent to suspend Section 338 has emerged in the days since. As of September 7, search results show no US counter-retaliation announcement or executive action in response to Canada's retaliatory list — the next market-moving event is whether Washington absorbs the September 8 effective date or announces a counter-escalation in the hours and days following. Trump's separate threat to impose 50% tariffs on all Canadian cars, trucks, auto parts, and steel effective January 1, 2027 adds a structural medium-term CAD negative beyond the immediate catalyst. USDCAD has been trading in the 1.39 area supported by the dual tailwind of structural CAD weakness from the tariff shock and the post-Warsh hawkish USD repricing.

implications.CAD: MAXIMUM CAD negative — US 50% tariffs live since Aug 22, Canada's full 700+ line retaliation effective 12:01am tonight (Sep 8), negotiations explicitly collapsed with no diplomatic off-ramp, Jan 1 2027 50% auto tariff threat adds structural overhang. USDCAD ~1.39, approaching/probing 1.3900. BoC rate hike expectations further compressed as tariff growth drag dominates. The immediate binary: US counter-retaliation post-Sep 8 = USDCAD accelerates above 1.40; US silence/absorption = modest near-term CAD relief toward 1.3850 but structural weakness remains. Expert commentary notes both governments have publicly committed in ways that make de-escalation structurally harder.
implications.USD: USDCAD directionally bullish from tariff shock, reinforced by post-Warsh hawkish USD repricing (Aug payrolls 162k/4.1% steady). Canada tariff shock adds modest USD safe-haven bid vs commodity bloc.
implications.MXN: USMCA credibility damage from US-Canada rupture keeps uncertainty elevated. Divergence in US-Mexico vs US-Canada bilateral progress adds uncertainty premium.
implications.EUR: Indirect — EURCAD likely bid on CAD weakness. Broader protectionism signal from Section 338 invocation has limited but non-zero EUR contagion.
implications.AUD: Commodity-bloc contagion — AUD trades defensively in acute CAD-shock episodes. AUDUSD subject to additional headwind from post-Warsh USD strength; vulnerable to further risk-off from US-Canada escalation spiral post Sep 8.
implications.NZD: Same as AUD. NZDCAD vol elevated. NZD defensive in commodity-bloc risk-off episodes.
implications.GBP: GBPCAD directional trade on CAD weakness. GBP otherwise dominated by BoE path and post-Warsh USD dynamics.
implications.JPY: CADJPY lower on dual pressure: CAD structural weakness from Section 338 tariff war plus structural JPY bid from BOJ Sep hike cycle and intervention regime.

themes.watchLevel: USDCAD 1.3900 is the immediate live test — a clean daily close above 1.3900 opens 1.4017-1.4021 (50-day EMA area) and then 1.4100. Post-Warsh USD tailwind (Aug payrolls 162k, 4.1% unemployment) makes 1.40 a plausible near-term target absent a diplomatic surprise. USDCAD 1.3800-1.3820 is near-term downside support; a close below 1.3780 would require a surprise diplomatic reopening. Sep 8 is the LIVE binary tonight: US counter-retaliation in the hours/days following = USDCAD accelerates above 1.40; US silence/absorption = modest near-term CAD relief rally toward 1.3850. Jan 1 2027 automotive tariff threat (50% on all Canadian cars, trucks, parts) is a structural medium-term CAD negative even if Sep 8 passes without further escalation. Theme ends only on: (1) formal re-opening of US-Canada talks with credible framework, or (2) Trump executive action suspending Section 338.

themes.title: USDJPY collapsed ~450 pips to ~155.72 — intervention/BOJ-hike surge Sep 3-4; Sep 17-18 BOJ hike ~73% priced; hard dual central bank binary week Sep 15-18 (FOMC+BOJ)
themes.summary: As of September 7, the USDJPY picture has transformed dramatically since the September 3 update. The pair, which was grinding at 160.33 with RSI at 70 on September 2, collapsed more than 450 pips in two sessions: on September 3 the yen surged more than 2%, at one point touching 155.28 — its strongest level against the dollar in approximately a month — driven by a combination of elevated intervention risk at the 160.00 line and accelerating market pricing of the September 17-18 BOJ hike. By September 4, USDJPY had partially stabilised near 156.02 with RSI recovered from oversold levels below 30 back up to approximately 58. TradingView data shows USDJPY near 155.72 as of September 7. The intervention regime, which spent approximately $58.97 billion in late July driving USDJPY to 155.27, has reasserted structural credibility: the pair rejected 160.40 decisively. The BOJ hike narrative remains fully intact. Governor Ueda's September 1 G20 signal and Hawkish board member Takata's September 2 Sapporo comments — calling for nimble hikes and describing 2026 as a turning point — lifted 2yr JGB yields to 1.83% (highest since 1995) and pushed market pricing to approximately 73% probability of a September hike. The BOJ's current rate is 1.00% (set June 2026); a September hike would take it to 1.25%. Reuters sources confirmed the BOJ is set to raise rates as soon as September and is considering a more aggressive thereafter pace than twice yearly. The pivotal dynamic now is the dual central bank binary week of September 15-18: FOMC decision on September 16 (with updated SEP and dot plot) is followed the next day by the BOJ September 17-18 meeting. These two events arriving in the same week — with the Fed potentially hiking and the BOJ potentially hiking simultaneously — represent the highest-volatility event cluster of the year for USDJPY. August payrolls printed 162,000 with unemployment steady at 4.1%, which keeps Fed hike probability elevated and limits how far the JPY rally can extend before FOMC. The September 10 Masu BOJ speech (if scheduled) remains the final pre-meeting BOJ communication.

implications.JPY: Three-pillar structural JPY support now decisively winning over carry forces: (1) Intervention regime — 160.00 rejected cleanly on Sep 2-3, USDJPY now ~155.72, regime credibility restored; (2) BOJ Sep hike ~73% priced, Ueda (Sep 1) and Takata (Sep 2) both delivered hawkish signals, 2yr JGB at 1.83% 30-year high; (3) Bessent-Ueda bilateral at G20 Asheville confirmed US-Japan policy coordination. Net: USDJPY now ~155.72 — intervention threat receded but BOJ Sep 17-18 binary is the dominant near-term driver. Sep 16 FOMC hike could provide a USD counterforce.
implications.USD: USDJPY has lost ~450 pips since Sep 2 as intervention/BOJ-hike bets overwhelmed carry. Post-Warsh hawkish repricing (Aug payrolls 162k/4.1%) provides USD support. Rate differential direction of travel is USD-negative vs JPY from BOJ side over medium term, but FOMC hike could narrow the gap trajectory.
implications.EUR: EURJPY under pressure from intervention mechanism and BOJ hike pricing. 2yr JGB at 1.83% 30-year high narrows EUR-JPY rate differential.
implications.GBP: GBPJPY under dual intervention and carry-unwind pressure — the Sep 3 yen surge hit all JPY crosses sharply.
implications.CHF: CHFJPY lower on intervention pressure. SNB in easing mode.
implications.CAD: CADJPY lower on dual pressure: CAD structural weakness from Section 338 tariff war plus JPY structural bid from BOJ hike cycle and intervention regime re-assertion.
implications.AUD: AUDJPY under intervention and carry-unwind pressure — dropped sharply Sep 3 alongside USDJPY. AUDUSD partially capped by post-Warsh USD strength.
implications.NZD: Same dynamic as AUD. NZDJPY under intervention and carry-unwind pressure.

themes.watchLevel: USDJPY ~155.72 is the current trading level after the 160.33 → 155.28 intervention/BOJ-hike surge. Key support: 155.27 (post-intervention low from late July); a break below 155.00 would signal further JPY strength toward 153-152. Key resistance: 157.00-158.00; a recovery above 158.00 without new BOJ/MoF pushback = carry traders re-engaging and partial unwind of hike pricing. BOJ Sep 17-18 is the hard binary: hike to 1.25% = USDJPY likely drops toward 152-150, 2yr JGB yields rally; no hike = JPY sells off sharply, 157-160 re-test, intervention regime faces fresh stress. FOMC Sep 16 hike (25bps to 3.75-4.00%) arriving one day before BOJ = rate differential temporarily widens, potential USDJPY short-squeeze before BOJ resolution. The dual FOMC+BOJ week (Sep 15-18) is the highest-impact FX event cluster of 2026. USDJPY below 153.00 = BOJ hike fully validated and JPY structural bull trend confirmed. Any MoF/Bessent statement disclaiming further intervention = theme ends immediately.

themes.title: Warsh hawkish repricing — Aug payrolls 162k/4.1% solid; Sep 11 CPI final pre-FOMC tiebreaker; Sep 16 FOMC hard binary; dual central bank week Sep 15-18 (FOMC+BOJ); 10yr UST ~4.79%
themes.summary: As of September 7, the Warsh hawkish repricing from Jackson Hole (August 28 keynote) remains structurally intact with CME FedWatch showing approximately 65-68% probability of a September 16 hike. August nonfarm payrolls, released September 4, printed 162,000 with the unemployment rate holding steady at 4.1% — a solid but not blowout result that Polymarket data confirms 'reinforced trader views favoring a 25 basis point federal funds rate hike.' Governor Christopher Waller has also been cited alongside Chair Warsh as providing hawkish signals. CPI inflation persists near 3.4% year-over-year with the federal funds target range at 3.50%-3.75%. The July FOMC vote was 9-3 to hold, with dissenters from Cleveland, Minneapolis, and Dallas regional banks all pushing for a hike — the most dissents since September 2016. J.P. Morgan Wealth Management expects a 25bp September hike; Goldman Sachs calls a September hike 'very unlikely' and expects a hold — a genuine split among major forecasters that reflects the genuine data dependence of this decision. Brent crude has been running near $89.70/barrel as of late August, adding a supply-side inflation variable. The FOMC July minutes confirmed that at longer horizons the market was fully pricing a 25bp hike by September. The critical pending event is the September 11 August CPI report — the last major inflation data point before the September 16 vote — which Polymarket notes 'could shift sentiment sharply depending on whether readings show continued cooling or renewed acceleration.' The September 16 FOMC decision arrives with updated SEP and dot plot, one day before the BOJ September 17-18 meeting, creating the most compressed dual central bank binary of the cycle. The stagflation risk (hot inflation from oil/tariffs, potential labor market softening) remains the key constraint on how aggressively further hike pricing can extend. Chicago PMI miss at 47.1 on August 28 and July's negative jobs print were growth caution signals, though August payrolls at 162k partially addressed the labor market concern.

implications.USD: DXY holding post-Warsh hawkish gains, 10yr UST near 4.79% (Jan 2025 high). Aug payrolls 162k/4.1% = CME FedWatch ~65-68% Sep hike steady. Sep 11 August CPI is the critical pre-FOMC tiebreaker: hot (core above 0.3% MoM or YoY above 3.3%) = Sep hike above 75%, DXY targets 100.50-101.00, EURUSD toward 1.1350-1.1450; soft (core at or below 0.2% MoM) = hike odds pull back toward 50%, DXY retraces toward 98.50-99.00. Sep 16 FOMC with updated SEP/dot plot is the hard policy binary.
implications.JPY: Warsh hawkish outcome creates cross-current against BOJ Sep hike narrative. USDJPY ~155.72 after the Sep 3-4 JPY surge — the dual Sep 15-18 week means both FOMC and BOJ land within 48 hours, creating maximum two-way USDJPY volatility risk. A Sep 16 FOMC hike followed by a Sep 17-18 BOJ hike could see initial USDJPY rally then sharp reversal.
implications.EUR: EURUSD has retraced from 1.1657 toward 1.1500-1.1550 on Warsh hawkish repricing. Sep 11 US CPI and Sep 16 FOMC are the next major EURUSD catalysts. ECB dynamics provide partial offset.
implications.GBP: GBPUSD subject to post-Warsh USD strength. Rate convergence story has partially shifted back in USD's favour. BoE's own path and UK data remain independent GBP drivers.
implications.CAD: Post-Warsh USD strength adds a second tailwind to USDCAD alongside the Section 338 tariff shock. USDCAD probing 1.39. Aug payrolls 162k = growth not collapsing, limits the stagflation constraint on hike pricing.
implications.AUD: AUDUSD partially reversed multi-month highs on Warsh hawkish USD repricing. Sep 11 CPI is a dual AUD catalyst: hot = USD bid keeps AUDUSD capped; soft = potential risk-on AUD relief.
implications.NZD: Same as AUD. NZDUSD retraced from recent highs on Warsh USD bid. RBNZ dynamics provide independent NZD input.
implications.CHF: USDCHF lifted by Warsh hawkish repricing. SNB easing mode limits CHF upside. CHF safe-haven bid provides partial offset in risk-off episodes.

themes.watchLevel: Sep 11 August CPI is the critical pre-FOMC tiebreaker (4 days away): hot (core above 0.3% MoM or YoY above 3.3%) = Sep hike above 75%, DXY toward 100.50-101.00, EURUSD toward 1.1350-1.1450; soft (core at or below 0.2% MoM per Goldman base case) = hike odds pull back toward 50%, DXY retraces toward 98.50-99.00. Sep 16 FOMC with updated SEP/dot plot is the hard policy binary: hike 25bps to 3.75-4.00% = full hawkish validation, DXY toward 101-102, EURUSD below 1.1300; hold with hawkish dots (2026 median above 4.00%) = partial validation; hold with unchanged dots = sell-the-news USD weakness. FOMC Sep 16 arrives one day before BOJ Sep 17-18 — a simultaneous hike from both central banks is an extraordinary USDJPY volatility scenario (initial USD bid, then massive JPY bid). 10yr UST at 4.79% is a key level — a sustained move above 4.85% signals full Sep hike plus Dec hike beginning to be discounted (consistent with Barclays double-hike call). DXY closing and sustaining below 98.00 = Warsh hawkish read fully unwound. Aug payrolls at 162k/4.1% has cleared the labour market bar for now — Sep 11 CPI is the final swing variable.
